text: Now we bring the query's source data into Power BI Desktop and shape it into a model DAX measures can actually use cleanly, not one flat imported table.

Import Orders, Customers, and Stores as separate tables, not the pre-classified query. The model needs the raw fact and dimension tables so measures can do their own time intelligence. Set correct data types at this step too, since auto-detected types are a common source of silent DAX errors downstream.

Build a proper Date dimension with a calendar function, and mark it as the official date table. Never rely on Power BI's hidden auto date and time, and turn that setting off so every visual uses this real table instead.

Relate Date to Orders on OrderDate, and Customers and Stores to Orders on their IDs, all single-direction, one-to-many. Bidirectional relationships are exactly the kind of thing that causes double-counting later, so they don't get added by default.
The model is a clean star schema now. Next: the DAX measures themselves, Active Customers, Churned Customers, and Churn Rate.
